add.title: LGBTQ rights in the United States (Wikipedia) — Housing of transgender inmates by state
add.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) stating that as of January 2021 California is the one state that allows transgender people to be housed in prison according to their gender identity, while New Mexico is the one state with separate facilities reserved for transgender people only; the article's U.S. state map legend codes California under 'Allows transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity' and notes the same context that federal policy returned to assigned-sex-at-birth placement after January 2017 guidance was rescinded. Placement axis: identity-based housing within the general population, with no trans-only separate facility documented for California.

add.title: LGBTQ rights in California (Wikipedia) — Prison policy
add.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) whose prison policy coverage documents that in 2015 California became the first state to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates, and cites KPBS reporting (2015) on 'Transgender In Prison: How California's New Guidelines Will Be Implemented' — CDCR's operational guidelines governing transgender inmates. Thin on the housing axis: the article confirms the identity-based care and guidance posture but contains no explicit statement of a trans-only unit or segregation practice.
